In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Eulerian subfilter scale velocity fluctuations are well correlated with the Lagrangian droplet velocity fluctuations for the droplet laden mixing layers considered here, and the subfilter scale thermodynamic fluctuations can be adequately predicted by the proposed scale similarity model.
the droplet dynamics in the mixing layer are strongly affected by the subgrid velocity fluctuations, but the subgrid fluctuations of temperature are less important.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a two-way coupled large eddy simulation is an accurate and efficient means of predicting droplet laden mixing layers undergoing transition to turbulence.
a subgrid model is needed to accurately capture the droplet drag, heat flux and evapotranspiration rates.
the subgrid velocity fluctuations may be neglected in the Eulerian gas-phase equations for Reynolds numbers up to at least Re=500.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the subgrid fluctuations are important to consider in large eddy simulations of droplet laden flows and the subgrid variance model proposed herein may be used to account for the effects of subgrid fluctuations on the droplets.
the droplet drag, heat flux, and evaporation rate may all be significantly overpredicted when subgrid fluctuations in the gas phase are neglected.
subgrid velocity fluctuations can have a significant effect on droplet dynamics, particularly for droplets with St∼1, and must be included when modeling the droplet drag forces in LES.
